text:
incident-bot: PAGING: runtime canary in us-west-2 showing 3x p50/p95 increase and a sustained throughput drop on model-serving pool. Page: #eng-oncall. Severity: P1.
Alex: I'm looking at canary traffic now — saw the alert ~30s ago. pulling canary dashboard.
Maria: noticed kernel fallback spikes on the canary slice. Kernel affinity looks wrong: several pods reported fallback to generic kernel A.
Alex: @Maria share the pod ids?
Maria: pod ids: svc-model-ckpt-7f9b, svc-model-ckpt-7f9c, svc-model-ckpt-7f9d. Logs show repeated kernel selection failures and batching stalls.
Sanjay: I'm checking the rollout config. We routed 10% to canary with the new prefetch/eviction change and a kernel selection flag. Possible misroute?
Katie: Customer impact — DataDog shows elevated tail latency for a dozen customers in prod-2 region, increased 429s for streaming sessions. Not global but a visible spike for some high-concurrency tenants.
Jordan: Repro snippet from canary pod logs:```ERROR kernel_selector: failed to bind optimized kernel for seq_len=2048; falling back to generic. batcher: waiting on kv-cache with timeout=200ms; queue_depth=72
TRACE batching: queued=40 inflight=4 max_batch=32
```
Alex: That queue_depth looks unusual — selector mis-evaluating sequence length distribution and causing large batches that blow past prefetch, leading to paging to disk in host kernel.
Sanjay: Rolling back the kernel-affinity flag for canary would be fastest. Can someone flip the kill-switch for the feature-flag controlling kernel routing? Flag key: runtime.kernelaffinity.v2
Maria: On it. Toggling kill-switch to OFF for canary traffic. `curl -X POST https://ff.redwood.internal/toggle?key=runtime.kernelaffinity.v2&env=canary&value=false`
ops-bot: Deploy bot: Feature flag runtime.kernelaffinity.v2 set to OFF for env=canary by Maria (request id 0a7c).
Alex: Observing metrics — p95 is starting to trend down after 90s. Throughput still low though.
Katie: Customer Impact check: 12 sessions had >2s tail latency; 4 sessions recorded streaming interruptions (retries kicked in). Support already notified and opened a priority ticket for affected accounts.
Jordan: Also seeing batching degen: batcher is forming huge batches because the canary's batch estimator returned inflated batch size. Could be due to the new prefetch heuristics returning stale stats.
Sanjay: Can we force the canary pool to use the stable batcher config? There is a route override we can apply: `routectl set canary batcher=stable`
Alex: I'll apply route override now to cut batch sizes.
Maria: Route override applied. ops-bot confirmed: routectl: override applied to canary: batcher=stable.
ops-bot: infra-bot: route override completed (id 9f3b). Canary traffic rebalanced.
Alex: Metrics: p95 down further, queue_depth back to ~10. Throughput recovering. Kernel fallback count dropping.
Sanjay: Good. I'm preparing a rollback of the canary config to the previous commit as a safer follow-up — want to fully revert prefetch heuristics. Should we do full rollback or keep overrides and monitor?
Jordan: My vote: rollback the canary commit that introduced both kernel-affinity and prefetch heuristics. Overrides are fine short-term but we should revert the risky change.
Katie: Support has the list of affected customers. Suggested communication: brief status + mitigation note; customers have been told we mitigated via rollback/override and monitoring.
Alex: I'll own the rollback. Scheduling immediate canary rollback (not prod rollback) to previous stable image: `deployctl rollback svc-model-canary --to=stable-2026-02-28`
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback job queued (job id ab12). Estimated completion ~2m.
Maria: Observability: adding a short-lived alert guard to prevent automated re-enable of the kernel-affinity flag in CI — we'll add a lock.
Sanjay: Handoff: I'm taking second shift for 30m while Alex stays to watch logs; if anything flares, escalate to eng-runtime paging channel and page infra-leads.
Alex: Thanks. I'm continuing to watch p99 and queued batches. Will post a follow-up when rollback completes and metrics stabilize.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback complete (job id ab12). Canary now on stable-2026-02-28.
Alex: Confirming metric baseline ~85% of normal p95, kernel fallback rates returned to baseline, no new 5xx surge.
Katie: Support note drafted and sent to affected tenants: short explanation + mitigation + ETA for full postmortem.
Sanjay: Initial impact estimate (preliminary): ~0.6% global requests affected during 10:24–10:36 window, 12 customers with noticeable tail latency, no data loss, some streaming retries.
Jordan: Postmortem action items: (1) Add canary preflight for batcher-estimator deltas > 2x (2) Lock auto-toggle for kernel-affinity flags until perf gates added (3) Add a soft limit on queue_depth to avoid paging loop.
Maria: I'll own (1) and (2). Alex will own (3) with eng-runtime.
Alex: Good. I'll also add a short runbook entry for on-call: when kernel-fallback spikes with batching stalls, apply route override, toggle kernel-affinity kill-switch, and rollback canary.
Sanjay: Closing notes: incident declared mitigated at 10:36. Assigning oncall follow-up meeting at 11:15 to walk through logs and finalize postmortem owners.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated. Severity lowered to P2. Follow-up meeting scheduled in #eng-runtime at 11:15.
Alex: Thanks everyone — great fast coordination.
Katie: I'll update the customer ticket with final mitigation timeline after the follow-up meeting.
Jordan: Leaving logs and links: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/in/canary/3115556666, Kibana: https://kibana.redwood/logs?query=svc-model-ckpt-7f9b, Rollback job: ab12.
Sanjay: handing off to oncall-next.
Alex: handoff ack.
---
Summary (for postmortem): short deploy introduced two changes together (kernel-affinity + prefetch heuristic) that combined to mis-estimate batch sizes, causing queue blowup and kernel fallback/paging on canary. Rapid mitigations: feature-flag kill-switch, route override to stable batcher, canary rollback. Customer impact limited to tail latency for small set of customers. Action items assigned above.
